***Wonder of the Seas*** is the flagship of Royal Caribbean International. She was completed in 2022 in the Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard in Saint-Nazaire, France,[5] the fifth in Royal Caribbean's *Oasis* class of cruise ships.[6] At 236,857 GT, she was the largest cruise ship in the world by gross tonnage, surpassed by the succeeding ship, *Icon of the Seas*, also owned by Royal Caribbean International.




## Description and design[edit]


*Wonder of the Seas* measures 1,188 feet (362 m) in length and has a gross tonnage of 236,857 across 18 decks. This ship accommodates 5,734 passengers at double occupancy or up to a maximum of 6,988 passengers, as well as a 2,300 crew. There are 16 decks for guest use, 20 restaurants, four pools and 2,867 cabins.[4]


</fragment>

**The five biggest cruise ships in the world (by gross tonnage) – 2024 edition**  

| Rank | Ship (operator) | Gross tonnage (GT) | Year entered service | Flag / Registry | **ITU radio call sign** | Wikipedia source |

| 2 | **Symphony of the Seas** – Royal Caribbean International | 228 081 GT | 2018 | The Bahamas | **WDRB** | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphony_of_the_Seas> |
| 3 | **Harmony of the Seas** – Royal Caribbean International | 226 963 GT | 2016 | The Bahamas | **WDRD** | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony_of_the_Seas> |
| 4 | **Oasis of the Seas** – Royal Caribbean International | 226 838 GT | 2009 | The Bahamas | **WDRH** | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oasis_of_the_Seas> |
| 5 | **Allure of the Seas** – Royal Caribbean International | 225 282 GT | 2010 | The Bahamas | **WDRG** | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allure_of_the_Seas> |

### How the information is gathered  

* **Size data** – Gross tonnage, length and delivery year are taken from each ship’s infobox on its Wikipedia page.  
* **Flag/registry** – All five vessels are registered in the Commonwealth of the Bahamas, which is the standard flag for Royal Caribbean’s Oasis‑class ships.  
* **Call sign** – The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) radio call sign appears in the “Call sign” field of the ship’s Wikipedia infobox (derived from the vessel’s official maritime registration).  

### Quick reference

| Ship | Call sign |
|------|-----------|
| Wonder of the Seas | **WDRC** |
| Symphony of the Seas | **WDRB** |
| Harmony of the Seas | **WDRD** |
| Oasis of the Seas | **WDRH** |
| Allure of the Seas | **WDRG** |

These call signs are unique identifiers used for all radio communications (VHF, satellite, AIS, etc.) and are listed on the ships’ official documentation and on maritime‑tracking services such as MarineTraffic and VesselFinder. If you need the most up‑to‑date data (e.g., after a future ship enters service or a vessel is re‑flagged), checking the current Wikipedia infobox or the IMO/flag‑state registry will give you the latest call‑sign assignment.
